```{r}
library(httr2)
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)

# 1. Create the request
req <- request("https://www.fruityvice.com/api/fruit/all") 

# 2. Perform the request and parse the JSON
resp <- req %>% 
  req_perform() %>% 
  resp_body_json()

# 3. Turn the list into a tidy tibble
fruit_data <- tibble(data = resp) %>%
  unnest_wider(data) %>%
  unnest_wider(nutritions) # Flatten the nested nutrition list

print(fruit_data)
```


```{r}
library(httr2)
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)

# --- CUSTOM FUNCTION ---
# Requirement: "at least one custom function"
# This extracts the birth year and calculates age, handling NA cases.
calc_award_age <- function(birth_date, award_year) {
  # If birth_date is missing, return NA to prevent errors
  if (is.na(birth_date)) return(NA_real_)
  
  birth_year <- as.numeric(substr(birth_date, 1, 4))
  age <- as.numeric(award_year) - birth_year
  return(age)
}

# --- 1. ACQUIRE DATA ---
# We use req_retry() to prevent that 502 error you saw earlier!
req <- request("https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureates") %>%
  req_url_query(limit = 50) %>%
  req_retry(max_tries = 3)

resp <- req %>% 
  req_perform() %>% 
  resp_body_json()

# --- 2. TIDY DATA ---
laureates_tidy <- tibble(raw = resp$laureates) %>%
  unnest_wider(raw) %>%
  # Laureates can have multiple prizes, so we unnest that list
  unnest_longer(nobelPrizes) %>%
  # FIX: Use names_sep = "_" to solve the "links" duplication error
  unnest_wider(nobelPrizes, names_sep = "_") %>%
  
  # Select the correct variables (note the nobelPrizes_ prefix)
  select(
    id, 
    name = fullName, 
    gender, 
    birth_info = birth, 
    award_year = nobelPrizes_awardYear, 
    category = nobelPrizes_categoryFullName
  ) %>%
  # Clean up the nested name/date fields using map_chr (Iteration!)
  mutate(
    name = map_chr(name, ~ .x$en %||% NA_character_),
    category = map_chr(category, ~ .x$en %||% NA_character_),
    # Handle the birth date which is nested inside birth_info
    birth_date = map_chr(birth_info, ~ .x$date %||% NA_character_),
    # Apply our custom function!
    age_at_award = map2_dbl(birth_date, award_year, calc_award_age)
  ) %>%
  # Remove the raw birth_info list column so we can save to CSV
  select(-birth_info)

# --- 3. SAVE DATA ---
# Requirement: "formed using write_csv()"
if (!dir.exists("data")) dir.create("data")
write_csv(laureates_tidy, "data/cleaned_nobel_laureates.csv")

# Quick check of the final tidy tibble
print(laureates_tidy)
```

```{r}
# --- STAGE III: ENHANCED TIDYING ---

laureates_tidy <- tibble(raw = resp$laureates) %>%
  unnest_wider(raw) %>%
  unnest_longer(nobelPrizes) %>%
  unnest_wider(nobelPrizes, names_sep = "_") %>%
  
  # Extract names and countries
  mutate(
    name           = map_chr(fullName, ~ .x$en %||% NA_character_),
    category       = map_chr(nobelPrizes_categoryFullName, ~ .x$en %||% NA_character_),
    award_year     = as.numeric(nobelPrizes_awardYear),
    birth_date     = map_chr(birth, ~ .x$date %||% NA_character_),
    
    # Grab Birth Country
    birth_country  = map_chr(birth, ~ .x$place$country$en %||% NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply your custom function for age
  mutate(
    age_at_award = map2_dbl(birth_date, award_year, calc_award_age)
  )

# --- NEW: COUNTING WINS BY COUNTRY ---
# We create a summary table of how many prizes each country has won
country_counts <- laureates_tidy %>%
  filter(!is.na(birth_country)) %>%
  count(birth_country, name = "total_country_wins")

# --- COMBINING DATA ---
# We join the counts back to the main table
final_nobel_data <- laureates_tidy %>%
  left_join(country_counts, by = "birth_country") %>%
  select(
    id, 
    name, 
    birth_country, 
    total_country_wins, # Now you have the "number" per country
    award_year, 
    category, 
    age_at_award
  )

# Save this enhanced version
write_csv(final_nobel_data, "data/nobel_with_country_stats.csv")

# Look at the top 10 countries by win count
print(country_counts %>% arrange(desc(total_country_wins)))
```

```{r}
# Project 2: Nobel Prize Data Acquisition
# Stage III Submission
# Partner 1 & Partner 2

library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

# --- 1. CUSTOM FUNCTION ---
# Requirement: "Your quarto file should contain at least one custom function"
# This function calculates the age of the laureate at the time of their award.
calc_award_age <- function(birth_date, award_year) {
  # Handle missing data or organizations (which have no birth date)
  if (is.na(birth_date) || birth_date == "") {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  # Extract year from YYYY-MM-DD
  birth_year <- as.numeric(substr(birth_date, 1, 4))
  age <- as.numeric(award_year) - birth_year
  return(age)
}

# --- 2. DATA ACQUISITION ---
# Requirement: "APIs (using httr or httr2)"
# We set limit to 1000 to get the full historical record.
print("Connecting to Nobel API...")
req <- request("https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureates") %>%
  req_url_query(limit = 1000) %>% 
  req_retry(max_tries = 5) # Crucial for 502 Bad Gateway errors

resp <- req %>% 
  req_perform() %>% 
  resp_body_json()

# --- 3. TIDYING & ITERATION ---
# Requirement: "create a tidy tibble" and "iteration techniques"
laureates_raw <- tibble(raw = resp$laureates) %>%
  unnest_wider(raw) %>%
  # Handle multiple prizes per person
  unnest_longer(nobelPrizes) %>%
  # Use names_sep to avoid the "links" column duplication error
  unnest_wider(nobelPrizes, names_sep = "_") 

# Process columns and apply custom function using purrr iteration
laureates_tidy <- laureates_raw %>%
  mutate(
    name          = map_chr(fullName, ~ .x$en %||% NA_character_),
    category      = map_chr(nobelPrizes_categoryFullName, ~ .x$en %||% NA_character_),
    award_year    = as.numeric(nobelPrizes_awardYear),
    birth_date    = map_chr(birth, ~ .x$date %||% NA_character_),
    # Reach into nested list for Birth Country
    birth_country = map_chr(birth, ~ .x$place$country$en %||% NA_character_),
    # Apply custom function via iteration
    age_at_award  = map2_dbl(birth_date, award_year, calc_award_age)
  )

# --- 4. COMBINING WITH COUNTRY STATS ---
# Create a summary of wins per country of origin
country_stats <- laureates_tidy %>%
  filter(!is.na(birth_country)) %>%
  count(birth_country, name = "total_country_wins")

# Join the count back to the main data
final_data <- laureates_tidy %>%
  left_join(country_stats, by = "birth_country") %>%
  select(
    id, 
    name, 
    gender, 
    birth_country, 
    total_country_wins, 
    award_year, 
    category, 
    age_at_award
  )

# --- 5. SAVE OUTPUT ---
# Requirement: "at least one .csv file (formed using write_csv())"
if (!dir.exists("data")) dir.create("data")
write_csv(final_data, "data/final_nobel_analysis.csv")

print("Success! Tidy data with 1000+ observations saved to data/folder.")
glimpse(final_data)
```
